messages:
leah: Quick heads-up — I opened a PR to consolidate Dedicated provisioning examples into a single page. Includes autoscale policy examples + migration notes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/handbook/pull/512

omar: Nice. Do we have a clear example showing the difference between 'scale_policy: conservative' and 'aggressive' for burst traffic? Customers keep asking for guidance.

leah: Not yet. Thinking small matrix + simple chart. Also need a snippet for SDK v2 (go) showing how to set min_replicas/max_replicas. @maya can you add the Go snippet?

maya: Yep. Will add a compact snippet and a one-line CLI example for rwctl. Also will add a note about isolation labels required for tenant-backed reserved pools.

sam-docs: Flag: current wording in the SLA section implies 99.95% for reserved — that conflicts with the SRE doc. Can we align to 'Reserved: 99.9% availability, 5-min recovery window' and call out best-effort for hosted? I'll open a follow-up PR.

sre-ops: Confirmed — reserved is 99.9% uptime for the control plane route and a per-request latency SLO of P99 under normal load. We'll give precise metric names.

infra-bot: CI: link-checker found 1 broken link -> /handbook/dedicated/old-terraform-examples. Suggested: /handbook/dedicated/terraform-examples-2025

omar: Also we should document eviction semantics in the autoscale section — e.g., which workloads get preempted first and how fallback routing works. A short example scenario would help.

maya: Added Go SDK snippet example:
```go
client := redwood.NewClient(apiKey)
pool, _ := client.CreateReservedPool(ctx, redwood.ReservedPool{
  Name: "analytics-pool",
  GPUType: "a100",
  ScalePolicy: redwood.ScalePolicy{ MinReplicas: 2, MaxReplicas: 8, Mode: "conservative" },
})
fmt.Println(pool.ID)
```
Also CLI one-liner: `rwctl reserved create --name analytics-pool --gpu a100 --min 2 --max 8`

leah: great — please also add a migration note: older `tenantLabel` key used to be `owner_id`, new key is `tenant_id`. Provide `rwctl tenant migrate-labels` example.

maya: done. Also added short QA checklist for after provisioning: `rwctl capacity status`, run sample inference, confirm KV-cache warmup.

sam-docs: tiny nit: change 'fallback routing' paragraph to specify that fallback may increase latency and token cost.

leah: updated. One more request — can we include a short 'what to watch in prod' section for SRE: e.g., P95 latency, queue depth, preemption count metrics, and alert thresholds. @sre-ops to confirm numbers.

sre-ops: Suggested thresholds: P95 < 120ms, queue_depth > 50 -> page, preemption_rate > 0.5% per hour -> warn. I'll paste metric names in the doc.

infra-bot: Build: succeeded (staging). Link-checker: 0 broken links. Spelling: 1 suggestion (changed 'scalling' -> 'scaling').

omar: LGTM. Thanks everyone. I'll merge after the follow-up PR from sam-docs lands for the SLA clarify.

leah: thanks team :tada: marking resolved.
